title: Molecular Dynamics of PPAR Nuclear Receptors: From Ligand Binding to Transcriptional Regulation.
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦PPAR核受体的分子动力学模拟，涵盖配体结合、构象动态及与RXR/DNA/共调节因子的互作，虽非典型TF-DNA结合位点预测，但涉及蛋白-DNA复合物建模与动态机制，方法可迁移至TF-DNA研究。
abstract: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARalpha, PPARbeta/delta, and PPARgamma) are ligand-regulated nuclear receptors that coordinate lipid metabolism, glucose homeostasis, inflammation, adipogenesis, differentiation, and disease-associated transcriptional programs. Although early structural models emphasized ligand-dependent stabilization of helix 12 (H12) and the activation function-2 surface (AF-2), evidence from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, NMR, HDX-MS, crystallography, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays supports a more complex conformational-ensemble mechanism. Apo and ligand-bound PPARs populate multiple functional substates whose distributions are shifted by ligands, RXR heterodimerization, DNA binding, co-regulators, post-translational modifications, and disease-associated mutations. This review summarizes MD and integrative structural studies of PPAR conformational dynamics, isoform-specific behavior, PPAR-RXR and co-regulator interactions, ligand entry, graded activation, inverse agonism, disease-associated mutations, and phosphorylation-dependent regulation. PPARgamma is the most extensively characterized isoform, whereas PPARalpha and particularly PPARbeta/delta remain comparatively underexplored by atomistic and enhanced-sampling approaches. MD is most informative when it extends beyond post-docking pose stability and is integrated with long-timescale sampling, free-energy methods, dynamic-network analysis, and experimental validation. Future simulations should increasingly model biologically realistic assemblies containing RXR, DNA, coactivators or corepressors, disease mutations, and post-translational modifications to connect ligand chemistry with receptor allostery, transcriptional output, and disease biology.
abstract_zh: 过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体（PPARalpha、PPARbeta/delta 和 PPARgamma）是配体调控的核受体，协调脂质代谢、葡萄糖稳态、炎症、脂肪生成、分化及疾病相关的转录程序。尽管早期结构模型强调配体依赖性稳定螺旋12（H12）和激活功能-2表面（AF-2），但来自分子动力学（MD）模拟、核磁共振（NMR）、氢-氘交换质谱（HDX-MS）、晶体学、诱变和生化实验的证据支持一种更复杂的构象集合机制。无配体态和配体结合的PPARs占据多种功能亚态，其分布受配体、RXR异二聚化、DNA结合、共调节因子、翻译后修饰及疾病相关突变的影响。本综述总结了PPAR构象动力学、亚型特异性行为、PPAR-RXR和共调节因子相互作用、配体进入、分级激活、反向激动、疾病相关突变及磷酸化依赖性调控的MD和整合结构研究。PPARgamma是表征最广泛的亚型，而PPARalpha，尤其是PPARbeta/delta，在原子级和增强采样方法方面仍相对未被充分探索。当MD超越后对接姿态稳定性，并与长时间尺度采样、自由能方法、动态网络分析和实验验证相结合时，其信息价值最大。未来的模拟应越来越多地模拟包含RXR、DNA、共激活因子或共抑制因子、疾病突变及翻译后修饰的生物学真实组装体，以将配体化学与受体变构、转录输出和疾病生物学联系起来。
